title: DatasetJsonlHeader
description: The first record of every training-record JSONL file exported by any conformant producer (world rules/conversations/truths, edit + generation + preference logs, QA labels, curated builder output). The file itself is referenced from a finetune job as a KMI asset with media type application/vnd.koine.dataset+jsonl (KFT §4.1, dataset.records[]); this header is also copied inline into the job manifest (dataset.header) so the provider can run the KFT §4.2 egress gate and the §7 spend estimate BEFORE fetching a byte. Guarantees the trust tier (KGP §7) + license class (§7.1) + egress class (§7.2) + provenance travel with the data. Every axis here is a FILE-LEVEL aggregate: egress is the most restrictive class over the file's rows, license their union, recordCount their number. A producer whose rows differ in class splits the file rather than widening the header (KFT §4.1).

datasetKind.description: e.g. rules-sft, nl-edit, generations, preferences, lore-qa, qa-labels

source.description: The emitting participant's KINP namespace (identity.md §3.4), e.g. worldsim | analyzer | refkb.

egress.description: Egress class of the file — the MOST RESTRICTIVE class over its rows (KGP §7.2, KFT §4.1/§4.2, FT-N). The gate reads this; a provider MUST NOT infer egress from `tier`, which is descriptive, not enforcing. Absent = the KGP §7.2 `exportable` default, so understating it is a producer bug rather than a permissive choice.

recordCount.description: Number of training rows after this header (FT-P). One asset id may hold ten rows or ten million, so this is the only cardinality a provider has for the KFT §7 admission-time spend estimate without transferring the file; it is re-checked on fetch.

provenance.description: emitter-specific: world ids, run ids, corpus DVC hashes.
